title: Power Automate process mining: tabs and customisable layouts in the process intelligence experience
summary: Hold: the table incorrectly says automation for reassigning a departed user's records is not documented; Microsoft documents a Dataverse action for that operation. The corrected admin path, automatic enablement and principal licensing figures are supported, and all six Learn pages that previously returned rate-limit responses opened successfully.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerapps-flow-licensing-faq#power-automate for the second statement.

claims.claim: The trial offers 100 MB of process mining capacity per process.
claims.quote: The trial offers limited process mining capacity of 100 MB per process.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The cited route is Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records.
claims.quote: Select the environment where the process is located. ... select **Settings**. ... Under **Users + permissions**, select **Users**. ... Select the leaving user. ... select **Reassign records**.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: API and automation cell
claims.claim: Automation for reassigning a departed user's Dataverse records is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Reassigns all records that are owned by a specified user to another security principal (user, team, or organization).
claims.fix: Remove controls[1] and its generated table row rather than printing an incorrect API absence; retain the verified UI reassignment instructions in prose. In Governance controls add: 'Microsoft also documents the Dataverse ReassignObjectsSystemUser action for reassigning all records owned by a specified user.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/reassignobjectssystemuser. This is a general Dataverse operation, not a process-only transfer.

claims.claim: The cited sharing page does not specify a named role required by the administrator performing the reassignment steps.
claims.quote: Searched: "process mining" "reassign" "administrator" "role". Read process-mining-share in full: it calls the actor an administrator, without naming an admin role. Its Environment Maker requirement concerns the target user, not the administrator.

claims.claim: Some Dataverse privileges are set by default so built-in roles can use process mining without further administrator action.
claims.quote: Some privileges are set by default in Dataverse. This allows built-in security roles to use the process mining capability without further actions from system administrators.

claims.claim: The experience documentation describes analysis and visualization rather than autonomous actions on tenant data.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "actions" "data" "sources". Opened studio-overview, tab-management and dynamic-layout. These describe human-driven analysis and configuration, not autonomous execution on tenant data.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no new data source introduced by this analysis interface.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "actions" "data" "sources". Opened studio-overview, tab-management and dynamic-layout; they describe process analytics and card configuration, not a new ingestion source introduced by this experience.

claims.claim: Layout changes can be saved to the tab.
claims.quote: Save changes made in edit layout mode by selecting **Save** when exiting edit mode.

claims.where: Governance guidance compared with Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist names security-role review, Conditional Access, public-tab management and capacity monitoring without corresponding control rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'List who holds the Environment maker, Process Mining User and administrator roles'; 'Check that any Conditional Access policy'; 'Review public tabs'; 'Watch Dataverse file capacity'. Table: only a missing feature switch and departed-owner reassignment.
claims.fix: The role-inventory, Conditional Access, public-tab review and Dataverse-capacity checklist steps have no corresponding controls-table rows. Remove these checklist bullets to restore table/checklist parity without adding unverified control rows; their documented factual background can remain in the body.
